name: Soninke
notes: Soninke (Serakhulle, Sarakolé), Soninke-Bozo branch of Mande, spoken by ~2.3 million people mostly in Mali and Mauritania, with communities across Senegal, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Ivory Coast and Burkina Faso. The Latin orthography follows the general West African convention shared with Bambara (bm) and Fula (ff): ⟨c⟩ = /tʃ/, ⟨j⟩ = /dʒ/, ⟨y⟩ = /j/, ⟨ñ⟩ = /ɲ/, ⟨ŋ⟩ = /ŋ/, ⟨x⟩ = velar/uvular fricative [x~χ]. Five vowel qualities /i e a o u/ contrast length, written by doubling the vowel letter. Word-initial prenasalized stops ⟨mb nd ng⟩ pattern with the same series in ff/wo/bm. This spec is quality:research: the letter-to-IPA correspondences are drawn from the cited Wikipedia consonant table (25 phonemes) rather than cross-checked page-by-page against Creissels's reference grammar; a prenasalized palatal digraph (⟨ny⟩) is mentioned in secondary summaries of the orthography but is omitted here pending a source that states its IPA value unambiguously, to avoid asserting an unconfirmed mapping.
